claims.text: Increasing scan speed during L-PBF of cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi promotes rapid solidification.
High-speed laser additive manufacturing will significantly refine the microstructure of AlCrFeNiSi.
High-speed laser additive manufacturing will suppress compositional segregation in AlCrFeNiSi.
High-speed laser additive manufacturing will suppress thermal gradients in AlCrFeNiSi.
High-speed laser additive manufacturing will reduce residual stresses in AlCrFeNiSi.
High-speed laser additive manufacturing will reduce defects in AlCrFeNiSi.
High-speed laser additive manufacturing will improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi.
Conventionally bulk-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi typically develops compositional segregation during slow cooling.
Conventionally bulk-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi exhibits residual stresses and mechanical defects caused by its thermal history.
A volumetric energy-density range of 50–80 J/mm³ has been reported for related medium-entropy alloys.
Higher scanning speeds increase the cooling rate during solidification.
Higher scanning speeds steepen thermal gradients during solidification.
Rapid solidification limits elemental diffusion and segregation between dendrites.
Higher scanning speeds reduce temperature gradients.
Reduced temperature gradients lower residual-stress development.
High-speed processing promotes a uniform fine-grained structure.
A uniform fine-grained structure enhances overall mechanical performance.
High-speed LAM AlCrFeNiSi will have higher tensile strength than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
High-speed LAM AlCrFeNiSi will have greater fracture strain than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
Scan speeds outside the optimal process window may cause part-density or porosity tradeoffs.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says high-speed processing suppresses thermal gradients, while the mechanism first says higher scan speed steepens thermal gradients and later says it reduces them.

The stated baseline is conventionally bulk-processed AlCrFeNiSi, but the experiment permits either bulk material or slower-scan LAM as the control; these controls test different processing contrasts and are not interchangeable.
